group: Normal validation – valid JSON, default customizer

cases.description: A well‑formed JSON instance that satisfies the schema. The customizer is null, so the method should behave like the overload without a customizer and return an empty validation result.
Same as above but with an explicit no‑op customizer. The method must invoke the overload with the provided Consumer and still return an empty set.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> contains at least one message about missing required property "id"
cases.description: The instance does not contain the required property defined by the schema, so the validator must return a non‑empty set with an appropriate message.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> contains exactly one message (fail‑fast mode)
cases.description: A customizer forces fail‑fast validation. The instance violates the schema (price is missing but not required, but suppose another rule like "minimum": 0 is added in the real schema). The validator should stop after the first error, returning a single message.
Passing a null JsonNode is not allowed; the method should validate its arguments and throw an exception.

cases.expected: RuntimeException with message "customizer failure" is propagated
cases.description: If the provided ExecutionContextCustomizer itself throws, the validate method must not swallow the exception; it should propagate it to the caller.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> is empty when instance matches pattern, non‑empty otherwise
cases.description: The customizer enables a specific validation feature (e.g., pattern properties). The test should verify that the validator respects the modified execution context.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> is empty regardless of pattern mismatch
cases.description: When the customizer disables the pattern‑checking feature, the validator should skip that rule, resulting in no errors even if the instance does not match the pattern.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> contains exactly two messages – one for "age" below minimum and one for "code" not matching the pattern
cases.description: The instance violates two independent constraints and the default execution context does not enable fail‑fast, so both errors must be reported.

group: Type mismatch – customizer disables type checking

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> is empty (type validator is disabled by the customizer)
cases.description: A customizer clears all enabled features, effectively turning off the type validator. Even though the instance is a string, no validation error should be produced.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> is empty (all array items satisfy the integer type)
cases.description: The schema expects an array of integers and the instance provides a correct array; validation must succeed.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> contains a message about element at index 1 not being an integer
cases.description: The instance contains a non‑integer element; the validator must report the type error for that specific array index.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> contains a type‑mismatch message because the instance is a string while the referenced schema expects an integer
cases.description: The validator must resolve the $ref correctly and apply the referenced integer type constraint.

group: Custom format validator – customizer registers format

input.value: execution -> execution.addFormatValidator("custom-email", (value, node) -> value.matches("^[^@]+@[^@]+\\.[^@]+$") ? Optional.empty() : Optional.of("Invalid custom email"))

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> is empty (the custom format validator accepts the provided email)
cases.description: A custom format validator is registered via the customizer; the instance complies with that validator, so no error is reported.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> contains exactly one message "Invalid custom email"
cases.description: The same custom format is registered but deliberately fails; the validator must surface the custom error message.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> is empty and SideEffectHolder.invoked == true after validation
cases.description: The test asserts that the provided customizer is actually executed (by toggling a static flag) and that normal validation still succeeds.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> contains a message whose text is in French (e.g., "la propriété requise 'name' est manquante")
cases.description: When the customizer changes the locale, the validator must produce messages in the selected language.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> is empty (an empty schema imposes no validation rules)
cases.description: A schema without any keywords should never produce validation errors regardless of the instance content.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or JsonSchemaException) is thrown due to malformed URI in $ref
cases.description: The schema contains a $ref with an invalid URI. When validate(JsonNode, ExecutionContextCustomizer) attempts to resolve the reference it should detect the malformed reference and throw an appropriate exception rather than silently ignoring it.
